Bug_Title: USELESS_STRING: Invocation of toString on an unnamed array (DMI_INVOKING_TOSTRING_ON_ANONYMOUS_ARRAY)
Bug_Details:
The code invokes toString on an (anonymous) array.  Calling toString on an array generates a fairly useless result
such as [C@16f0472. Consider using Arrays.toString to convert the array into a readable
String that gives the contents of the array. See Programming Puzzlers, chapter 3, puzzle 12.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the showBug() method where toString() is invoked on an anonymous integer array. This calls Java's default toString() method which returns a class name and hashcode, not the actual array content.
Trigger_Explanation: The generated JUNIT test case calls the showBug() method of the UselessStringBug class. The result of the method is then compared to the string '[1, 2, 3]'. Since the showBug() method incorrectly invokes toString() on an anonymous integer array, the result will be a class name and hashcode, not the actual array content. This causes the assertNotEquals() method to fail, triggering the bug.
